name: Glacier National Park
blurb: Whitebark pine, grizzlies and wolves in the Crown of the Continent.

tip.title: Lose the whitebark pine
tip.text: Blister rust is killing whitebark pines. Set Whitebark pine to -100% and watch red squirrels, Clark's nutcrackers and the grizzlies that raid squirrel caches.

notes: The story and why it matters come from the Wikipedia articles listed below (Glacier National Park (U.S.), Pinus albicaulis, Mountain goat). Individual species and links have not been checked one by one. Feeding links that match a GloBI (Global Biotic Interactions) record are marked in the node details, with a link to the records. A few links were added from GloBI records.

nodes.desc: Short, intense alpine summers drive plant growth, and the growing season ends early at high elevation.
Fire is a regular part of the park and burns several thousand acres in an average year. It opens forest and clears ground for sun-loving plants.
Break down dead plants, animals and carcasses, returning nutrients to the soil.
A tall wildflower that thrives on burned and disturbed ground. GloBI records mule deer and elk feeding on it.
A berry-bearing shrub of open slopes. Bears, birds and browsing ungulates use its fruit and leaves.
High-elevation pine whose fat seeds feed nutcrackers, squirrels and bears. Blister rust has killed many trees in the park.
Forest squirrel that stores cones and seeds in middens. Bears raid middens for whitebark pine seeds.
Browses and grazes in forests, with a white winter coat. It is the main prey of Canada lynx.
Corvid that harvests whitebark pine seeds and caches them across the slopes. Uneaten caches grow into new trees.
Large grazer and browser of grasses, plants, leaves and bark. It is the main large prey of wolves and its carcasses feed scavengers.
Grazes grasses and forbs on open slopes and rocky ground, moving down to winter ranges.
Slender forest carnivore. GloBI records show it eating red squirrels and snowshoe hares.
Hare specialist; snowshoe hares make up most of its diet and lynx numbers follow the hare cycle. Listed as threatened in the US.
Scavenges large mammal carcasses such as deer and elk, and also hunts ground squirrels, marmots and hares.
Clever omnivore and scavenger that feeds at carcasses and takes small prey.

nodes.name: Grizzly bear
nodes.desc: Omnivore of lilies, berries, roots, ground squirrels, whitebark pine caches and elk. The Glacier area is a core of the northern Rockies population.
Eliminated from the park by the 1930s and recolonized naturally from the 1980s; preys on elk and other ungulates.

story: Glacier National Park in Montana covers more than a million acres, with over 130 named lakes and more than 1,000 plant species. It is the center of the Crown of the Continent Ecosystem. About 150 large glaciers existed here in the mid-1800s, and only 25 were active by 2010.
matters: The park still has almost all its original native plants and animals. Scientists have estimated its active glaciers could disappear by 2030 if current climate patterns continue.
